introBody: Whole-body cryotherapy exposes the body to a pool of extremely cold air for up to three minutes. Sessions are fully supervised and designed to be safe, fast, and part of your performance and recovery routine.
Step into extreme dry cold at approximately -160°F. Every session is efficient, controlled, and built around your schedule.

faqs.question: What is Whole Body Cryotherapy / Full Body Cryotherapy?
faqs.answer: Whole body cryotherapy is a treatment that exposes the client's or patient's whole body—in most cases with the exception of the head—to a pool of extremely cold air for two to three minutes. Whole-body cryotherapy is often also referred to simply as cryotherapy.

faqs.question: What temperature is cryotherapy?
faqs.answer: In whole-body cryotherapy, temperatures generally range between -80°C / -110°F and -110°C / -160°F in electric machines, and between -110°C / -160°F and -160°C / -250°F for liquid-nitrogen systems. These temperatures are achieved with coolants such as liquid nitrogen or with refrigerants.

faqs.question: What is cryotherapy used for?
faqs.answer: Cryotherapy is used for conditioning of the human body in sports recovery, physiotherapy, beauty, and wellness. Many clients use cryotherapy as part of their regular recovery routine.

faqs.question: What are the benefits of cryotherapy for athletes?
faqs.answer: Cryotherapy boosts energy levels, speeds up recovery, and has a generally positive effect on the body.

faqs.question: Does cryotherapy burn fat?
faqs.answer: Cold exposure may stimulate thermoregulation and brown-fat activity, which plays a role in heat production and energy use. However, cryotherapy is not a standalone fat-loss treatment. It is best used alongside exercise, nutrition, and other Apex recovery modalities to support a complete metabolic-health program.

faqs.question: What are the benefits of cryotherapy for weight loss?
faqs.answer: Cryotherapy greatly improves the effects of exercise and, from users' experiences, can also help the user keep going by alleviating after-effects of intense activity that may otherwise reduce motivation for further exercise.
